words.gloss: a ruler of a cruel sceptre

literal: If [he] is a cruel-sceptred ruler behaving doing fear-causing [deeds], certainly quickly [he] will be ruined.
translation: If a king rules with a cruel sceptre, performing deeds that cause fear to his subjects, his ruin is certain and will come quickly.
modern: மக்களுக்கு அச்சம் தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்து ஆட்சி நடத்தும் கொடுங்கோலனாக ஒரு அரசன் இருந்தால், அவன் நிச்சயம் விரைவில் அழிவான்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the swift and inevitable downfall of a tyrannical ruler. The term 'வெங்கோலன்' refers to a ruler with a hot or cruel sceptre, symbolizing tyranny. When such a ruler acts in a way that causes fear ('வெருவந்த') among his subjects, his power cannot endure. The poet emphasizes that his destruction is not just possible, but both certain ('ஒருவந்தம்') and rapid ('ஒல்லை'). The key message is that governance through fear and oppression leads directly to a ruler's immediate ruin.
